solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Powder starts to act like cocaine in gut

indicators.note: 'in' tells us the starting letters go inside the word for gut

parts.note: tum is an informal word for the stomach or gut

indicators.note: 'starts to' asks for the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: A warning about some white powder that behaves like cocaine once it reaches your stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Talcum is a fine soft powder dusted on the skin after bathing.

clue.text: Passage the writer will read aloud

indicators.note: words read aloud are judged by how they sound, not how they are written

parts.note: the writer refers to the setter, I, so 'the writer will' is I'LL

explanation.surface: An author announces that they will give a public reading of a passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' looks like a piece of text for the reading, but it is the definition: a walkway between seats.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats, as in a church or theatre.

clue.text: Prickly sharp pain — something done by needle

parts.note: a prickly person is irritable, or cross
a stitch is a sudden sharp pain in the side

explanation.surface: An irritable person with a stabbing pain, blamed on something done with a needle.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross-stitch is an embroidery stitch made of two crossing diagonal stitches, worked with a needle.

clue.text: Caring male with different lady's case

parts.note: other means different, as in 'the other way'

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, so its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A caring man pictured beside a different woman's suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' keeps only the outside letters of lady, L and Y; the 's just joins them to the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Motherly behaviour is warm and protective, the kind of caring associated with a mother.

clue.text: Wear out guitar, endlessly rocking in outskirts of Fringe

indicators.note: 'in' says the rocked letters sit inside the outskirts of the next word
the outskirts of a word are its outer letters, first and last
rocking shakes the letters up into a new arrangement
endlessly cuts off the final letter of the word guitar

explanation.surface: A musician thrashes a guitar to death at the Edinburgh Fringe festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims guitar to GUITA, 'rocking' rearranges that to ATIGU, and 'in' places it between F and E, the outskirts of Fringe.
explanation.definitionFit: To fatigue someone is to tire them, to wear them out.

clue.text: Loud boozers, these Europeans

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical direction for loud
a boozer is British slang for a pub, so boozers are inns

explanation.surface: A group of rowdy drinkers turn out to be from a particular European country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boozers' looks like drinkers but means pubs: boozer is British slang for a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Finns are the people of Finland, a European nation.

clue.text: Grog — never good — inebriate consumes in private

indicators.note: one who consumes something takes it inside, so these letters go in the middle

parts.note: an inebriate is a drunkard, a toper

indicators.note: never good means every G (good) is dropped from the word

parts.note: grog is rum and water, the sailor's drink

explanation.surface: A drunk downs bad grog in secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in private' reads as 'secretly', but private is the definition: the soldier. 'never good' means no G survives, so both go.
explanation.definitionFit: A trooper is a private soldier in a cavalry or armoured regiment.

clue.text: Mark, perhaps Mike, penning us evangelical tunes

parts.note: Mark is one of the four Gospels, hence the 'perhaps'

indicators.note: penning encloses something, so the next letters go inside

parts.note: mic is short for microphone, often called a mike

explanation.surface: Two people called Mark and Mike write religious songs for us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mike' looks like a second name beside Mark, but it is a microphone.
explanation.definitionFit: Gospel music is an evangelical Christian song tradition rooted in African-American churches.

clue.text: Both daughters avoiding downgraded ham?

indicators.note: avoiding means leaving those letters out of the word

parts.note: downgraded means demoted
D is the abbreviation for daughter, so both daughters are two Ds

explanation.surface: Two daughters steer clear of a cheaper cut of ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' looks like meat but is the verb: to overact. Taking both Ds out of DEMOTED leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to overact, and to emote is to show emotion in an exaggerated theatrical way.

clue.text: One sharing opportunity with tea

parts.note: room means scope or opportunity, as in 'room for improvement'
mate is a South American herbal tea

explanation.surface: Someone who shares a pot of tea when the chance arises.
explanation.definitionFit: A roommate is someone you share a room or flat with.

clue.text: Bloke with trio playing without emotion

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are being played around with into a new order

explanation.surface: A man sits in with a trio playing music, coldly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges the letters of BLOKE and TRIO together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something robot-like behaves mechanically, showing no feeling.

clue.text: Disc unaltered for Manchester band

parts.note: a disc is round, so it is shaped like the letter O
something left unaltered is left as is

explanation.surface: A record released with no changes by a famous group from Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Oasis was the Britpop group from Manchester led by the Gallagher brothers.

clue.text: One poem written in associate's flat

indicators.note: written in means these letters are put inside the next word

parts.note: a mate is an associate or companion
I is the Roman numeral for one
a sonnet is a fourteen-line poem

explanation.surface: A single poem composed in a friend's apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: A maisonette is a flat on two floors with its own entrance, in British usage.

clue.text: Working in steel capable of being stretched

indicators.note: working suggests the letters being worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A metalworker notes that steel can be drawn out when worked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' rearranges the letters of IN STEEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Tensile describes a material that can be drawn out or stretched under tension.

clue.text: Pat Boone, in customs on US ground, going up unexpectedly

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are broken up and remade

explanation.surface: The singer Pat Boone, in a US customs hall, suddenly goes up in flames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' rearranges all the letters of PAT BOONE IN CUSTOMS ON US. 'going up' looks like rising but means bursting into flame.
explanation.definitionFit: Spontaneous combustion is catching fire with no outside spark, so going up in flames unexpectedly.

clue.text: Have second thoughts about donkeys kept in reserve

indicators.note: kept in means held inside the next word

parts.note: asses are donkeys

explanation.surface: A farmer reconsiders the donkeys held back on a reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassess something is to evaluate it again, giving it second thoughts.

clue.text: Stop media manipulation happening

parts.note: PR, public relations, is the business of managing the media
a happening is an event

explanation.surface: A call to halt the spin doctors managing a news event.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevent something is to stop it from happening.

clue.text: Phlegmatic firm accepting contract's termination

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the letter goes inside the word for firm

parts.note: firm means solid

indicators.note: the termination of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: An unflappable company signs off on the end of a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'termination' gives T, the last letter of contract (the 's only joins), and 'accepting' puts it inside SOLID.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolid and phlegmatic both describe a calm, unemotional temperament.

clue.text: Ingenious restricting opponent in bit of bridge

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the clever word holds the other inside it

parts.note: ingenious means clever
anti is a noun for someone opposed to something

explanation.surface: A clever card player blocks an opponent during a hand of bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' suggests the card game, but it is the structure.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantilever is a projecting beam fixed at one end, used to build some bridges.

clue.text: Atlantic island rising above the horizon

definitions.meaning: ... Island is a British territory in the South Atlantic
in astronomy, ... is a star's rising above the horizon

explanation.definitionFit: Ascension names the South Atlantic island and also the act of rising, used of heavenly bodies coming up.

clue.text: Five gold cases aunt lost somewhere in Pacific

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: cases means wraps round, so gold's letters enclose the others

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: lost means astray or confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An aunt goes missing with five gold boxes somewhere out in the Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' rearranges aunt into NUAT before the gold goes round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanuatu is an island nation in the South Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Performer in Carmen cast gathering precious lace and diamonds

indicators.note: gathering means collecting in, so the rearranged letters hold the others
cast can mean thrown about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: orris is a lace made of gold or silver thread
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: A singer in Bizet's opera Carmen wears gold lace and diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like the opera's cast but rearranges Carmen into MANCER; the lace and diamonds go in after its M.
explanation.definitionFit: A Morris dancer performs traditional English folk dances with bells and sticks.

clue.text: Cut wood to support seats

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so it comes last

parts.note: your seat is your bottom, or rump
teak is a hardwood

explanation.surface: Cut some timber to prop up the chairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like an instruction to the carpenter, but it is the definition: a cut of beef.
explanation.definitionFit: Rump steak is a cut of beef taken from the hindquarters.

clue.text: One has Washington involved in droll approach to House

indicators.note: involved in means placed inside, so the letters sit within the word for droll

parts.note: dry humour is droll, quietly witty
said by the speaker, 'one has' becomes I'VE
WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state

explanation.surface: Someone takes a quietly humorous line in Washington about approaching the House.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' with a capital suggests Congress, but it just means a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A driveway is the private road leading up to a house.

clue.text: Northerner drunk touring clubs

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the word for drunk goes round the letter

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A drunk northerner makes the round of the nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' puts SOT round C. A Scot is a 'northerner' from Britain's point of view.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scot comes from Scotland, the northern part of Britain.

clue.text: Pawnbroker at last makes a million in America

parts.note: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word makes

explanation.surface: A pawnbroker finally strikes it rich, making a million in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Sam is the personification of the United States government and nation.

clue.text: Modern coffee variety always served across road

parts.note: a latte is a kind of milky coffee
ay, a variant of aye, is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A trendy café serves up a variety of coffee from across the street.
explanation.walkthrough: AY for always is an old or poetic usage, as in 'for ay'. The pieces are simply set side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Latter-day means belonging to recent times, a modern version of something older.

clue.text: Sex in the City with no sex recalled personal dispossession

indicators.note: 'in' places the first piece within the abbreviation for the City

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London
sex is Latin for six, which is VI in Roman numerals

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: A sexless remake of the TV show Sex and the City, remembered fondly.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Sex' is Latin for six, giving its Roman numeral; the reversed pair reads TION.
explanation.definitionFit: An eviction is the legal removal of a tenant from their home, a dispossession of a person.

clue.text: Musical concerned with Post Office elevated worker

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevated means lifted up, so the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical
re means concerning or about

explanation.surface: A musical about the Post Office gets a promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' reverses EVITA, RE and PO together, which in a down entry reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An operative is a worker, especially one operating machinery, or a secret agent.

clue.text: Lops head off flowering plant

indicators.note: off means wrong or gone bad, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener cuts the top off a plant in bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges the letters of LOPS HEAD. 'Lops head off' reads as pruning, which hides the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a lily-family plant with white or yellow flowers, linked in legend with the Elysian fields.

clue.text: Sauciest hint outrageously passionate

indicators.note: outrageously suggests wild, unruly behaviour, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: The rudest innuendo, delivered with shocking eagerness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outrageously' rearranges the letters of SAUCIEST HINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Enthusiastic means showing intense and eager interest, full of passion for something.

clue.text: Discontinue drinking Médoc, maybe following beastly complaint

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so these letters go inside the word for discontinue

parts.note: to sever is to cut off or discontinue
Médoc is a Bordeaux red, an example of wine
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Someone gives up drinking claret after catching some nasty bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beastly' looks like 'nasty' but means of beasts, pigs here.
explanation.definitionFit: Swine fever is a contagious viral disease of pigs, a complaint of animals.

clue.text: Cool parties outside or not outside

parts.note: in means fashionable, or cool

indicators.note: outside means placed round, so the word for parties goes round the other letters

parts.note: dos is an informal word for parties

explanation.surface: Trendy parties held out in the open, or else not out in the open.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue uses 'outside' twice: once as the container signal and once in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Indoors means inside a building, so not outside.

clue.text: Creep around behind seven others when earl departs for shining tower

indicators.note: around means going round, so the word for creep surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a louse is a contemptible person, a creep

indicators.note: the earl departing means the letter standing for him leaves the word

parts.note: whoever is behind seven others is placed eighth

explanation.surface: A sneak creeps round behind a group of seven, after a nobleman leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking E from EIGHTH leaves IGHTH, the piece the creep goes round.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighthouse is a tower with a bright lamp that shines to guide ships.

clue.text: Murmur about a strange blemish or rash

indicators.note: about means round, so the word for murmur goes round the other letters

parts.note: a hum is a low murmur
rum is British slang for strange or odd
a scar is a blemish on the skin

explanation.surface: A doctor mutters about an odd skin mark or rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like a skin complaint but means reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: Harum-scarum means reckless and impetuous, acting rashly without thought.

clue.text: Say Montgomery, Alabama, east of grassland swamp

indicators.note: in an across clue east is to the right, so these letters come after

parts.note: a field is an area of grassland
a marsh is a swamp
AL is the postal abbreviation for Alabama

explanation.surface: Montgomery, Alabama, lies east of some meadow and marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Montgomery, Alabama' reads as the state capital, but Montgomery is the British wartime commander; 'Say' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Bernard Montgomery was a British field marshal, the army's highest rank, so he is an example.

clue.text: Blooming radiation emission: uranium sent out

indicators.note: sent out means dismissed, so that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: fluorescence is light given off by a substance absorbing radiation
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A physicist describes radiation given off as uranium is ejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent out' removes U from FLUORESCENCE. 'Blooming' reads as a mild British curse but means flowering.
explanation.definitionFit: Florescence is the process or time of flowering in a plant.

clue.text: Check on progress: cramp eased with massage finally working

indicators.note: working means set into motion, so the letters are worked into a new order
finally picks the last letter of the word massage

explanation.surface: A runner's cramp eases with a massage, and they make good progress at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives E from massage, and 'working' rearranges it with CRAMP EASED.
explanation.definitionFit: A speed camera checks the speed at which vehicles progress, catching those going too fast.

clue.text: In French, one barbed remark is unbecoming

parts.note: a means one, as in 'a pound'
a dig is a pointed, barbed comment

explanation.surface: A cutting remark made in French is not quite the done thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infra dig' is short for Latin infra dignitatem, beneath one's dignity.
explanation.definitionFit: Infra dig describes behaviour beneath one's dignity, unbecoming of a person of standing.

clue.text: Tarzan in sunless Staffordshire location?

parts.note: a sunless sky is grey
Stoke-on-Trent is a city in Staffordshire, an English county; the question mark notes the shortening

explanation.surface: Tarzan turns up in a dreary town in the English Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: Tarzan is Lord Greystoke in the novels, so the name stands for him. STOKE is Stoke-on-Trent, a pottery city in Staffordshire, a Midlands county.
explanation.definitionFit: In Edgar Rice Burroughs' novels Tarzan is heir to the title Lord Greystoke.

clue.text: Hit cross from the right — this allows an opening

indicators.note: read from the right means read backwards, right to left

parts.note: to bonk is to hit, informally
a rood is a cross, especially a crucifix in a church

explanation.surface: A boxer lands a right cross to create an opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the right' reverses BONK and ROOD together. 'cross' and 'Hit' set up a boxing picture, but cross is the church rood.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning a doorknob lets you open a door, so it is the thing that allows an opening.

clue.text: Majestic European prince regularly absent

indicators.note: letters regularly absent means every other letter is dropped, keeping alternate ones

explanation.surface: A European royal who keeps missing official engagements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly absent' keeps P, I and C, the first, third and fifth letters of prince.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic means grand and heroic in scale, imposing like something majestic.

clue.text: Management set out to receive bribes on reflection?

indicators.note: reflection in a mirror shows things backwards, so the letters are reversed
to receive means to take in, so the word for set out holds the other inside

parts.note: laid means set out, as a table is laid
sops are small gifts given to placate someone, bribes

explanation.surface: Bosses lay down a policy on taking backhanders, and then think again.
explanation.walkthrough: The container comes first, giving LASOPSID, and only then is the whole read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Having something at your disposal means having it to manage or control as you choose.

clue.text: Chemical, produced outside Lima, taken in for literary monster

indicators.note: taken in means held between, so the built-up piece goes inside the other two

parts.note: Mr Hyde is the monster side of Dr Jekyll in Stevenson's novella

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the word for produced goes round the letter

parts.note: made means produced
L is Lima in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A chemical made outside Lima, Peru, is smuggled in for Mr Hyde.
explanation.walkthrough: The inner container gives MALDE, which then sits between the other two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Formaldehyde is a pungent gas used in solution to preserve specimens, a well-known chemical.

clue.text: Direct Beowulf perhaps, cryptically represented?

indicators.note: the clue asks us to show the poem's description cryptically, by writing one part inside the other

parts.note: Beowulf is written in Old English, OE
Beowulf is an example of verse, which is what 'perhaps' points to

explanation.surface: A question of how to stage a production of Beowulf.
explanation.walkthrough: Beowulf is the classic Old English poem; the clue asks for that description shown cryptically, one part written inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise or direct the work of others.

clue.text: Established batting fails after wicket for this team?

indicators.note: after means the following letters come behind the first

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for wicket
in cricket a side batting is said to be in
dies means fails or stops working

explanation.surface: A cricket team's established batting order collapses after a wicket falls.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a cricket side, and the West Indies plays Test cricket; 'this team?' points to the answer as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The West Indies is a Test cricket team drawn from the Caribbean nations.

clue.text: Print court document initially abridged

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word document

parts.note: an abridged text has been cut

explanation.surface: A shortened legal document is printed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests a law court, but here it is the verb to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodcut is a print made from a design carved into a block of wood.

clue.text: Small vessel raised after master abandons her

indicators.note: after means the raised piece follows the other
abandons means leaves behind, so those letters drop out

parts.note: a master is a schoolteacher
something raised is up

explanation.surface: A small boat is hauled up after the captain leaves her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandons' takes HER out of TEACHER to leave TEAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacup is a small vessel for drinking tea, and the vessel/ship double meaning hides it.

clue.text: Pilot Officer embraces Scottish John softly

indicators.note: embraces means hugs, so the first word's letters wrap round the second

parts.note: PO is the RAF abbreviation for Pilot Officer
Ian is the Scottish form of John

explanation.surface: An RAF officer gently hugs a Scotsman named John.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano is the musical direction meaning play softly or quietly.

clue.text: Wind is turning — enormous bird caught out at first

indicators.note: turning means turned around, so the two letters read backwards

parts.note: the roc is a giant mythical bird from the Arabian Nights
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of the word out

explanation.surface: The wind changes direction, and a huge bird is caught out early on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses IS to SI. 'caught out' looks like a cricket phrase, but caught is C and 'at first' gives O from out.
explanation.definitionFit: The sirocco is a hot dusty wind blowing from North Africa across the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Reportedly destroyed old page in open book

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken or heard, so we go by the sound of the words

parts.note: destroyed is wrecked, and O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An ancient page in a book is said to have been ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: WRECKED plus O, said out loud, gives the answer's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The recto is the right-hand page of an open book, opposite the verso.

clue.text: Stopping act, artist on page very debauched

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so these letters fill the middle of the word for act

parts.note: a deed is an act

indicators.note: in an across clue 'on' means the following piece comes after

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist working on a page interrupts a very decadent act.
explanation.definitionFit: Depraved means morally corrupt, utterly debauched.

clue.text: Doctor round surgery to wilt from exhaustion

parts.note: a round shape is like the letter O
an op is a surgical operation

explanation.surface: A doctor on their rounds wilts with tiredness after surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: To droop is to sag or flag, as a tired person or wilting flower does.

clue.text: Moderate with Labour's leader drawing support

parts.note: to ease something is to moderate it

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter

explanation.surface: A moderate approach wins backing from the Labour Party's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing support' looks like political backing, but it is a stand that holds a drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand that holds a canvas or drawing board while an artist works.

clue.text: Noesis and success with format on developing literary style

indicators.note: developing means unfolding into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer's style grows from understanding and success with a fresh format.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' rearranges NOESIS, SUCCESS, FORMAT and ON. Noesis is a philosophical word for intellectual understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Stream of consciousness is a narrative style that follows a character's flowing thoughts, as in Joyce or Woolf.

clue.text: Potter's friend mostly solitary individual

indicators.note: mostly means not all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a solitary is someone who lives alone, a hermit
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A potter's pal is a loner, for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' looks like a maker of pots, but it is Harry Potter. 'mostly' trims HERMIT to HERMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermione Granger is one of Harry Potter's two closest friends in J.K. Rowling's books.

clue.text: Intro missed from straightforward record in dance

indicators.note: with its intro missed, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: an honest person is straightforward
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: The opening is cut from a plain record of a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intro missed from' drops H from HONEST to leave ONEST.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-step is a ballroom dance popular in the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Prone position Rabbula periodically occupies

indicators.note: something that occupies a space sits inside it, so these letters go within the other word

parts.note: a lie is a position, as the lie of a golf ball

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Rabbula, the fifth-century bishop of Edessa, now and then assumes a lying position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'periodically' takes A, B and L, the even letters of Rabbula. 'Prone' looks like lying face down but means inclined to.
explanation.definitionFit: Liable means likely or inclined to do something, just as prone does.
